_about: THE EMPEROR'S DIARY (EN) — English adaptation of Korean longform ep04 '아내를 잃은 밤' (YouTube qpaS2nWMBng). Owner 2026-11-13 00:27 KST: English long-form one a day from the Korean back catalogue. Same shots, clips, sound and music as ../ep04.py + ../ep04_spec.py; English voices (voices_en.json: N Ron, M Robert, MAID Margot, SENATOR Carl), English on-screen text, Western modern scenes (e4en_*). Meditations quotes: George Long (1862, public domain), lightly modernized. No mention of a Korean channel anywhere.

lines.h1: Winter, the year 175. Below the Taurus Mountains, in a small village in Cappadocia called Halala.
lines.h_maid: Majesty... the Empress... she is gone.
lines.h2: Faustina. His wife of thirty years. That night, the most powerful man in the empire was left alone in his tent.
lines.m_h1: A morning without her is coming.
lines.s1: A few months earlier, a false rumor swept across the empire. The emperor, people said, was dead.
lines.s2: Avidius Cassius, the general who ruled the East, believed it, and declared himself emperor. The same rebellion from our first story.
lines.s3: The revolt was over in three months. The emperor set out on the long road east to calm the shaken provinces, and the Empress Faustina went with him.
lines.s4: And on the way home, in a small village beneath the mountains, she fell ill.
lines.d1q: Late at night, a phone call from the care home. Your father has just passed away.
lines.d1q2: Even at the funeral home, the same thoughts keep circling. If only I had visited last weekend. If only I had stayed on the phone a little longer.
lines.d1a: That night, the same kind of thoughts must have flooded the emperor's mind.
lines.d1b: If I had never brought her on this long road. If I had called the physician just a little sooner.
lines.d1c: Until dawn, he sat beside the lamp. Then he opened his diary.
lines.m1a: My child is sick. That, I can see.
lines.m1b: But that my child is in danger, I do not see.
lines.m1c: Say nothing more to yourself than what first appearances report.
lines.d1d: He separated what had happened from the story he was adding to it. That his wife was gone was a fact. That it was all his fault was a story he had added.
lines.d1e: !What happens is one thing. It's the story we build on top of it that breaks us.
lines.d1t: At first light, a letter from Rome reached the tent.
lines.d2q: One month after losing her husband, people keep asking how she'll go on. But all she can see is the empty place he left behind.
lines.d2q2: The words meant to comfort her only cut deeper. Let it go. Life is for the living.
lines.d2a: The letter carried a cruel rumor. That the empress had secretly written to Cassius and encouraged the rebellion.
lines.r_sen: They say the empress stirred up the revolt. That's why the gods took her.
lines.d2b: The emperor did not answer the rumor. Instead, he wrote to the Senate, and asked them to honor his wife as a goddess.
lines.m2b: That I had such a wife, so obedient, so affectionate, and so simple.
lines.m2c: I am grateful that I had a wife so affectionate and so simple.
lines.d2c: He did not count what he had lost. He counted what he had been given. A bride of fifteen and a groom of twenty-four, and thirty years together. The children they raised. The battlefields they crossed.
lines.d2d: !As long as we count what they left us, the ones we lost live again inside us.
lines.d2t: A few days later, a pyre was raised on the hill outside the village.
lines.d3q: The day you said goodbye to the dog who shared fifteen years of your life. Everything in the house is the same, and everything is different.
lines.d3q2: Someone says, it was only a dog. But to you, it was fifteen years of mornings and evenings.
lines.d3a: The funeral fire for the empress rose into the winter sky. The soldiers lowered their standards and stood in silence.
lines.d3b: This was not his first goodbye. He was a father who had already buried several of his children.
lines.m3a: What was yesterday becomes something else today, and what is today will become something else tomorrow.
lines.m3b: And nature delights in this change.
lines.m3c: Loss is nothing else but change.
lines.d3c: To him, death was not disappearing. It was a return to the great flow of nature. He did not say, don't grieve. He said, don't believe it is only an ending.
lines.d3d: !The time you shared does not vanish. It changes shape, and stays inside you.
lines.d3t: The morning after the funeral, before dawn, the emperor had to rise again.
lines.d4q: A month after losing his wife. From the bus window on the way to work, the world goes on as if nothing happened, and it feels cruel.
lines.d4q2: Still, every morning, he irons his own shirt with clumsy hands and walks out the door. What she always did for him, he now does alone.
lines.d4a: Outside the tent, his secretaries and officers were waiting. The cities of the East, shaken by the rebellion, were waiting for his judgment.
lines.d4b: He took to the road again. And to most of the cities that had joined the revolt, he gave pardon instead of punishment.
lines.m4a: In the morning, when you rise unwillingly, say this.
lines.m4b: Was I made to lie in the bedclothes and keep myself warm?
lines.m4c: I am rising to do the work of a human being.
lines.d4c: It doesn't mean you must defeat your grief. It means carrying your grief, and going back to one small task for today. For him, that task was caring for an empire.
lines.d4d: !Cooking a meal. Leaving the house. Watering a plant. Those small things are what lift us back up.
lines.d4t: And not long after, the emperor began one more thing, for her.
lines.d5q: A year since her mother died. And she still hasn't deleted Mom from her phone.
lines.d5q2: The longing hasn't faded. She just doesn't know where to put it.
lines.d5a: He renamed Halala, the village where his wife had died. Faustinopolis. The city of Faustina.
lines.d5b: And in her name, he founded a fund to support girls from poor families. People called them the Girls of Faustina.
lines.m5a: Take pleasure in one thing, and rest in it.
lines.m5b: Passing from one act for others to another.
lines.m5c: From one kind act to the next. Find your joy there.
lines.d5c: He did not keep his longing locked inside. In his wife's name, he helped someone else's tomorrow. And so his grief became something good left in the world.
lines.d5d: !A small scholarship, given in her mother's name. That is how longing becomes someone else's tomorrow.
lines.c1: The emperor who sat alone in his tent that night lived on for several more years, and guarded the empire until the end.
lines.m_c1: The morning without her came. And I rose.
lines.r1: When you lose someone you love, here are the five ways the emperor left in his diary, once more.
lines.t0: Tonight, before you sleep, try just these three things.
lines.r9: !The ones we lose do not come back. But what they gave us keeps us living, even today.
lines.o1: If this story helped, a like and a subscribe help us make the next one. Thank you.
lines.o2: In the next story, we'll open the emperor's diary again.
